verses.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
verses.2: Should the wise answer with the wind? Should the fullness of knowledge fill his belly?
verses.3: Should one who is upright argue with words that do not matter, with arguments that bring no benefit?
verses.4: You too have abandoned fear, and you speak with words before the face of God.
verses.5: For your sins have prepared your mouth, and your tongue has chosen the words of the cunning.
verses.6: Your own mouth will condemn you, and your lips will accuse you.
verses.7: Were you the first man to be born? Did you come before the hills?
verses.8: Have you listened to the secrets of God, and has wisdom come to you personally?
verses.9: What do you know that we do not know? What understanding do you possess that we lack?
verses.10: Both the aged and the experienced among us are wiser than your father in days.
verses.11: You are but slightly touched by the consolations of God, and you have spoken greatly beyond your measure.
verses.12: What has seized your heart? What has made your eyes blaze?
verses.13: For you have turned your spirit against God, and you have brought out such words from your mouth.
verses.14: What is a human that he might be just? Or what is a child of a woman that he might be innocent?
verses.15: Even in the holy ones he does not trust, and the heavens are not clean in his eyes.
verses.16: How much more then one who is abhorred and rejected, a man who drinks injustice like water.
verses.17: Listen to me, my friend, and let me tell you what I have seen and declare to you.
verses.18: These things the wise have declared, and their ancestors did not conceal them.
verses.19: The earth was given to them alone, and no outsider has passed among them.
verses.20: All the days of the wicked are full of turmoil, and the years of the wicked are numbered for the wicked.
verses.21: A voice of terrors is in his ears; even in peace, the destroyer will come to him.
verses.22: He will not believe he has escaped from darkness, and he is already marked for the sword.
verses.23: He wanders for bread, not knowing where to find it; he is unaware that the day of darkness is in his hand.
verses.24: He is seized by trouble and distress; like a king waiting to be captured, he is surrounded.
verses.25: For he has stretched out his hand against God and has grown proud before the Almighty.
verses.26: He runs toward him with arrogance, with the fatness of his back as a shield before him.
verses.27: For he has hidden his face in fat, and he has made his face gluttonous upon his thighs.
verses.28: He dwells in ruined cities and enters houses that no one lives in; those he prepared for others will now drive him out.
verses.29: He will not grow rich, nor will his wealth endure; he will not cast his shadow on the land.
verses.30: He will not escape from darkness; his root will dry up, and his fruit will be blown away by his own breath.
verses.31: Let him not trust in his riches, for they will vanish into nothing.
verses.32: His harvest will be cut down before its time, and his fruit will not be sweet.
verses.33: He will be torn like a grapevine before its time, and he will be cast off like an olive branch.
verses.34: For a people of scoffers are a gathering of fire, and a fire consumes the tents of those who take bribes.
verses.35: He conceives trouble and gives birth to evil, and his belly stores up deceit.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 6: "accuse you" reflects the poetic parallelism to the mouth's condemnation.  
- v. 10: "wiser than your father in days" captures the comparison of age and wisdom.  
- v. 11: "consolations of God" is a poetic rendering of the idea of divine comfort.  
- v. 20: "numbered for the wicked" reflects the Hebrew's focus on the inevitability of judgment.  
- v. 30: "blown away by his own breath" is a poetic rendering of the Hebrew, emphasizing self-destruction.
